key_insight: With limited labeled mammograms, standalone CNNs delivered the best dense breast tissue segmentation and accuracy–compute balance, outperforming transformer and prompted MedSAM approaches.
clinical_relevance: More accurate dense-tissue segmentation could support breast-density assessment in mammography research; this study does not evaluate cancer drug discovery or clinical outcomes.
method: Compared classical segmentation, CNN/U-Net and transformer models under a unified evaluation protocol.
Evaluated self-supervised pre-training, fine-tuning strategies and loss functions.
Tested MedSAM with box, breast-region and CNN-generated dense prompts.
evidence_signal: The study used 596 expert-annotated images and 20,000 unlabeled mammograms; a density-calibrated hybrid loss reduced test percent-density MAE from 14.8 to 11.8 percentage points.
watch_item: The small annotated dataset limits conclusions about generalizability, and MedSAM performance was highly sensitive to prompt quality.
paper_title: Dense Breast Tissue Segmentation under Limited Annotation: Comparing CNNs, Transformers, Self-Supervision, and Prompting
